title: Copper ion-induced MYH9 polymerization executes cuproptosis.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: No data files exist to open. I checked NCBI E-utilities elink from PubMed ID 42735689 to GEO, SRA, BioProject, BioSample, PubChem assays and PMC (all five returned empty link sets); Zenodo (0 hits); PRIDE, the proteomics repository (keyword searches for 'cuproptosis' and 'MYH9' returned only unrelated 2019-2026 submissions from other groups); ProteomeXchange (redirect, no dataset); and the Europe PMC datalinks endpoint, whose only entries are antibody RRIDs (Research Resource Identifiers, e.g. RRID:AB_3714886) and a Mouse Genome Informatics reference stub. The publisher's full text and PDF both return HTTP 403.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything scientific: that MYH9 (myosin heavy-chain 9) is a cuproptosis executioner, that copper binding drives its polymerization, that HThPA acts via the nuclear receptor Nur77, and that drug-resistant tumours and clinical samples have higher copper. All of this comes from the 200-word abstract only, since no full text was retrievable.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. There is no dataset anywhere. Zero accessions in GEO, SRA, BioProject, BioSample, PRIDE, ProteomeXchange or Zenodo; Europe PMC reports hasSuppl=N and no PMCID, so the supplementary file list is not retrievable; cell.com returns HTTP 403 for both the full text and the PDF. Crossref records a CC BY 4.0 licence, so the article is nominally open, but the publisher blocks programmatic access and no files are deposited in any repository.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. This is a mechanistic cell-biology paper whose results are western blots, microscopy images, viability curves, mouse xenografts and immunoprecipitation-mass-spectrometry hits. There is no table with a prediction target in a column; any label (e.g. 'this protein polymerizes on copper binding') would have to be constructed by hand from figure panels.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not assessable: no files. The only machine-readable identifiers linked to the paper are 25 antibody RRIDs, which are reagent catalogue codes, not model inputs.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessable: no data table to carry units.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL by construction. A single-mechanism study of one protein (MYH9) with cell-line and xenograft experiments yields tens of conditions, not the ~1,500 labelled rows the checklist requires. No row count could be verified because no file exists.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially passes only because there is nothing to download.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not assessable: no download, no API record and no supplement to compare against the paper's claims.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessable. The measurements described (copper binding, polymerization, acetylation by DLAT) are genuine wet-lab readouts, not model outputs, but none of them are released as data, so provenance cannot be traced to a file.

existing_models.score_and_split: Reported in Nature Chemical Biology (2022); applied to four prokaryotic proteomes and predicted 4,849 candidate metalloproteins. Exact split and metric not retrieved, only the abstract-level summary.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved — I read search summaries, not the discussion.

existing_models.score_and_split: Benchmarked alongside PRIME-seq and M-Ionic; a 2026 comparison reports their precision-recall and ROC curves are near-identical, which the authors read as the language-model approach having saturated at current data sizes.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Further gains from protein-language-model methods are 'challenging under the current data size and comparable model architectures' — i.e. more data, not better architecture, is the bottleneck.

backbone.hardware: Not applicable — there is no labelled data to fit a head on.

integration.partner_dataset: None usable. The paper contributes one gene (MYH9, UniProt P35579) and one compound (HThPA), which is a join of size one, not a dataset.
integration.join_key: UniProt accession (in principle), but with a single protein there is nothing to join.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: a single-protein mechanistic finding has no table to combine with a large resource.

controls.positive_control: None available — no data to run a control on.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: this paper releases no machine-readable data, so no model can be trained or evaluated from it.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequence to predict which proteins polymerize and kill the cell when they bind copper.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would need many proteins labelled for copper-triggered polymerization. This paper supplies exactly one such protein (MYH9), so the number of usable training examples is 1.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a given protein aggregates or polymerizes on copper binding, with the truth coming from wet-lab assays (turbidity, electron microscopy, cross-linking). This paper reports those assays only for MYH9, in figures, not in a table.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Cancer-drug developers working on cuproptosis (copper-dependent cell death) would want to know which other proteins are copper-polymerization targets; but this paper gives one data point, which is a hypothesis, not a training set.

ml_idea: The only idea the paper suggests — predict copper-induced protein polymerization from sequence — would need a labelled set of proteins assayed for copper-driven aggregation. That set does not exist here or, as far as my searches found, anywhere public. The adjacent task that does have data (predicting metal-binding sites) is already served by at least three open models (MetalNet, LMetalSite, PinMyMetal), and this paper adds nothing to their training data.

effort.compute_note: No compute estimate is meaningful because there is no data to load. Nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Query NCBI elink from the PubMed ID to GEO, SRA, BioProject and PMC, plus PRIDE and Zenodo. All returned empty in under two minutes, which killed the candidate immediately.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails outright: the paper deposits no data in any repository (GEO, SRA, BioProject, PRIDE, ProteomeXchange and Zenodo all empty), has no PMC copy so its supplement is unreachable, and the publisher returns HTTP 403. A2 and A5 fail too — it is a single-protein mechanistic study whose results are blots, images and xenografts, so the prediction target would have to be built by hand from figures and would amount to one labelled example.
